question: The Commission has stated to Parliament that Israeli beneficiaries of Horizon Europe cannot be considered in breach of Article 14 of the Horizon Europe Model Grant Agreement merely because they are established in Israel and that measures must be based on the beneficiary’s conduct rather than on the actions of the State of Israel1.

Previously, however, the Commission proposed a partial suspension of the Horizon Europe Partnership Agreement based on Israeli violations of Articles 2 and 79(2) of the EU-Israel Association Agreement.

Under such a suspension, legal entities established in Israel, irrespective of their individual conduct, would no longer be eligible to participate in Horizon Europe calls linked to the EIC Accelerator funding programme. While more limited, the latter proposal aligns better with the Commission’s March 2022 general suspension of cooperation with Russian beneficiaries2. 1.

Does the Commission confirm that legal consequences may be imposed on Israeli entities based on conduct attributable to the State of Israel, provided that the legal basis is the violation of Article 2 of the Association Agreement?
If so, why has the Commission shifted back to presenting the issue as one of beneficiary conduct rather than one of restrictions resulting from the conditions of an international agreement?
